title: Job's Hope Sinks Toward the Grave
overview: Job, sick and mocked by his friends, asks God to vouch for him and then wonders aloud whether his hope will simply die with him.

parts.label: Near death and mocked (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: Job feels his life running out and the grave already waiting for him. Worse, the friends who came to comfort him now surround him with scorn.

parts.label: Asking God to vouch for him (vv. 3-5)
parts.note: In a legal case, someone could guarantee a person by putting down a pledge or shaking hands on it, and Job asks God himself to do this because no one else will. He says God has closed his friends' minds, and warns that betraying a friend for gain harms one's own children, though the exact sense of verse 5 is uncertain.

parts.label: Shamed and wasting away (vv. 6-9)
parts.note: Job says God has made him a byword, a proverb people point to as an example of disgrace, and people spit in his face, a deep public insult. He says decent people will be shocked and will hold on to what is right, though readers differ on whether he means this sincerely or bitterly.

parts.label: Challenge to the friends (v. 10)
parts.note: Job dares his friends to come back and argue again. He doubts any of them will say anything wise.

parts.label: Night called day (vv. 11-12)
parts.note: Job says his days are over and his plans and heart's hopes are broken off. The Hebrew of verse 12 is hard; many read it as Job mocking his friends for insisting light is near when darkness is closing in, while others read it as his own fading longing.

parts.label: Hope buried in the dust (vv. 13-16)
parts.note: Sheol was the shadowy place of the dead, and by calling decay his father and the worm his mother or sister, Job says the grave is now his closest family. He asks whether the hope his friends promised will simply go down into the dust with him.

think: When someone is suffering, what makes words of comfort feel hollow rather than helpful?
